meanings: (Buddhism) to free oneself of worldly worries

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
⺼ (flesh, body) — 脱 relates to taking something off the body.
兑 (duì) gives a sound close to tuō, sharing a related initial.

example.hanzi: 冥想帮助他从压力中解脱出来。
example.pinyin: míngxiǎng bāngzhù tā cóng yālì zhōng jiětuō chūlái.
example.english: Meditation helped him free himself from stress.
example.fact: The practice of mindfulness meditation traces back over 2,500 years to early Buddhist traditions in India, but modern neuroscience has confirmed real physical effects: MRI studies show that eight weeks of regular meditation can measurably shrink the amygdala, the brain region that drives the stress response.

components.note: 忄 (heart, mind) — 懦 (cowardly, weak-willed) is a trait seated in the heart.
需 (xū) gives a sound only distantly related to nuò today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 面对危险时逃跑的人常被称为懦夫。
example.pinyin: miànduì wēixiǎn shí táopǎo de rén cháng bèi chēngwéi nuòfū.
example.english: Someone who runs away in the face of danger is often called a coward.
example.fact: The 'fight-or-flight' response was first named in 1915 by physiologist Walter Cannon, who found that a surge of adrenaline prepares an animal's body to confront a threat or flee it within seconds. Freezing in place, sometimes mistaken for cowardice, is actually a third survival strategy — many prey animals, from rabbits to deer, freeze first because sudden stillness can make a predator lose track of them.

components.note: 责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'
忄 (heart) — 怪 relates to a feeling of the heart, describing something strange or blameworthy that stirs unease.
圣 (here read guài, unrelated to the homographic 圣 meaning 'sacred') matches the sound of 怪 exactly.

example.hanzi: 他为迟到的事责怪自己的车。
example.pinyin: tā wèi chídào de shì zéguài zìjǐ de chē.
example.english: He blamed his car for being late.
example.fact: In 1977, psychologist Lee Ross coined the term 'fundamental attribution error' to describe humans' tendency to blame other people's failures on their character while excusing our own identical mistakes as caused by circumstance — a bias later replicated across many different cultures.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这场战争终于迎来了终结。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng zhànzhēng zhōngyú yíngláile zhōngjié.
example.english: This war finally came to an end.
example.fact: The Hundred Years' War, despite its name, actually spanned 116 years (1337-1453) and only ended when French forces retook Bordeaux, the last English stronghold on the European continent.

components.note: 八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
事 pictures a hand holding a forked stick used as an official tally or record-keeping tool, tying the character to its meanings 'affair, matter' and 'to serve.'

example.hanzi: 我和他共事了十年。
example.pinyin: wǒ hé tā gòngshìle shí nián.
example.english: I have worked together with him for ten years.
example.fact: Leafcutter ant colonies divide labor so precisely that some workers specialize purely as living trash compactors, packing waste into underground chambers, while others cultivate the fungus gardens the colony depends on for food — a division of labor among genetically identical sisters that biologists have studied for over a century.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雅 originally named a type of crow, later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'elegant, refined.'
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'

example.hanzi: 西雅图以经常下雨著称。
example.pinyin: xīyǎtú yǐ jīngcháng xiàyǔ zhùchēng.
example.english: Seattle is known for its frequent rain.
example.fact: Despite its reputation for rain, Seattle actually receives less annual precipitation than New York City, Miami, or Houston — its fame for grey weather instead comes from the sheer number of overcast days, over 200 a year, caused by the Pacific jet stream pushing low clouds against the Cascade and Olympic mountains.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
及 pictures a hand (又) reaching out to grab a person (人) fleeing ahead — the image of catching up to someone, the source of 及's meaning 'to reach, to arrive at.'

example.hanzi: 快点,我们要来不及了!
example.pinyin: kuài diǎn, wǒmen yào láibují le!
example.english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!
example.fact: Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains have averaged an annual delay of less than one minute per train since the network opened in 1964, including time lost to earthquakes and typhoons — a level of precision that requires station staff to plan schedules down to fifteen-second increments.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 狂 originally described a mad, rabid dog, extending to 'wild, crazy.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to kuáng, having drifted apart over time.
灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè

example.hanzi: 球迷们对这场比赛表现出狂热的热情。
example.pinyin: qiúmímen duì zhè chǎng bǐsài biǎoxiàn chū kuángrè de rèqíng.
example.english: The fans showed fanatical enthusiasm for this match.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, a single rare tulip bulb could sell for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman, with some bulbs reportedly trading for entire houses — one of the earliest documented speculative bubbles in economic history.

meanings: to provide financial or material support

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 这家公司赞助了奥运会代表队。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī zànzhùle àoyùnhuì dàibiǎoduì.
example.english: This company sponsored the Olympic team.
example.fact: Coca-Cola has sponsored every Olympic Games since 1928, making it the longest continuously running corporate sponsorship in the history of sports.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 那位老人其实是政界的大人物。
example.pinyin: nà wèi lǎorén qíshí shì zhèngjiè de dàrénwù.
example.english: That old man is actually a big shot in politics.
example.fact: British anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed in the 1990s that the human brain can maintain only about 150 meaningful social relationships at once, a limit he linked to the size of the neocortex — which may help explain why a handful of 'important people' loom disproportionately large within any one person's social world.

components.note: 土 depicts a mound of earth resting on the ground — a simple picture of soil, giving 土 its meaning 'earth, soil, land.'
The bowl-shaped body of an old stemmed serving dish.
A lid or rim on top of the dish.

example.hanzi: 妈妈用土豆做了一道好吃的菜。
example.pinyin: māma yòng tǔdòu zuòle yī dào hǎochī de cài.
example.english: Mom made a delicious dish with potatoes.
example.fact: The potato was first domesticated more than 7,000 years ago by indigenous peoples near Lake Titicaca in the Andes, and Peru alone still cultivates over 4,000 distinct varieties today, ranging in color from white to deep purple.

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
氵 (water) — 泽 names a marsh or pool, a body of water.
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'

example.hanzi: 他去新泽西读大学。
example.pinyin: tā qù xīnzéxī dú dàxué.
example.english: He went to New Jersey for college.
example.fact: Despite its small size, New Jersey has the highest population density of any U.S. state and is also home to more diners per square mile than anywhere else in the country, a legacy of the state's role as a 20th-century manufacturing and rail hub.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

艹 (grass) sits atop 萨's simplified form; the character originally named a plant but has been repurposed almost entirely as a phonetic symbol for transcribing foreign sounds like 'sa,' as in place and personal names.
其 (qí) is close in sound to sī, sharing the character's historical reading before later sound shifts.
斤 (an axe) — 斯 originally depicted splitting wood with an axe; the meaning later shifted entirely to a grammatical particle and a phonetic symbol used in transliterations.

example.hanzi: 德克萨斯是美国面积最大的州之一。
example.pinyin: dékèsàsī shì měiguó miànjī zuìdà de zhōu zhī yī.
example.english: Texas is one of the largest states in the US by area.
example.fact: Texas was an independent republic for nearly a decade (1836-1845) before joining the United States, and it even had its own navy and its own currency, called Texas dollars, before annexation folded it into the Union as the 28th state.

components.note: 衣 (cloth) — 裂 describes cloth tearing apart.
列 (liè) is an exact match for the sound of 裂.
Thread — sewing uses thread.
Gives the sound féng, matching the character's other reading (as a verb meaning 'to sew').

example.hanzi: 墙上出现了一条裂缝。
example.pinyin: qiáng shàng chūxiànle yī tiáo lièfèng.
example.english: A crack appeared on the wall.
example.fact: Kintsugi, a centuries-old Japanese art form, repairs cracks in broken pottery with gold-dusted lacquer rather than hiding them, treating the fracture as part of the object's history instead of a flaw to conceal.

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他大学学的是土木工程。
example.pinyin: tā dàxué xué de shì tǔmù gōngchéng.
example.english: He studied civil engineering in college.
example.fact: The Roman Pantheon, completed around 128 AD, still holds the record for the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — a feat of engineering that relied on a concrete mixture graded lighter toward the top, using volcanic pumice instead of heavier aggregate.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 我们的相遇纯属偶然。
example.pinyin: wǒmen de xiāngyù chúnshǔ ǒurán.
example.english: Our meeting was purely by chance.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 purely by accident, after noticing that mold had contaminated a petri dish he'd left uncovered and was killing the bacteria growing around it — a chance observation that launched the age of antibiotics.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 邻居家的狗整晚叫,真烦人。
example.pinyin: línjū jiā de gǒu zhěngwǎn jiào, zhēn fánrén.
example.english: The neighbor's dog barked all night, so annoying.
example.fact: Mosquitoes' high-pitched whine is the sound of their wings beating up to 800 times per second, and only female mosquitoes bite — they need the protein in blood to develop their eggs, while males feed solely on nectar.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng
讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng

example.hanzi: 你给我们讲讲这次旅行的故事吧。
example.pinyin: nǐ gěi wǒmen jiǎngjiǎng zhè cì lǔxíng de gùshì ba.
example.english: Tell us a bit about the story of this trip.
example.fact: Oral storytelling predates writing by tens of thousands of years, and some Aboriginal Australian oral traditions have been shown by geologists to accurately describe coastline changes from sea-level rise that occurred more than 7,000 years ago, passed down across roughly 300 generations.

components.note: 無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'
亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.

example.hanzi: 她在舞会上找到了一个好舞伴。
example.pinyin: tā zài wǔhuì shàng zhǎodàole yī gè hǎo wǔbàn.
example.english: She found a good dance partner at the dance party.
example.fact: The tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century, blending African, European, and South American musical traditions, and was considered so scandalous at first that some ballrooms banned it outright.

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
当 is the simplified form of 當, which combined 田 (a field) with 尚 (shàng, phonetic) — a field's value being 'matched' or 'equivalent' gave rise to meanings like 'to act as' and 'appropriate, timely.'

example.hanzi: 他正当我们需要帮助的时候出现了。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngdāng wǒmen xūyào bāngzhù de shíhòu chūxiànle.
example.english: He appeared just when we needed help.
example.fact: Arctic terns time their migration so precisely that they arrive at breeding grounds just as the local insect population peaks, completing a round trip of roughly 70,000 kilometers each year — the longest annual migration of any animal on Earth.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 堕 describes falling down toward the ground.
陏 (Suí) gives a sound distantly related to duò, having drifted apart over time.
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 他因为赌博而逐渐堕落。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi dǔbó ér zhújiàn duòluò.
example.english: He gradually degenerated because of gambling.
example.fact: Roman emperors of the 3rd century AD progressively debased the denarius, the empire's standard silver coin, from nearly pure silver to barely 5% silver content within decades — a slow monetary collapse that historians link to the runaway inflation and instability of the empire's darkest years.

components.note: 羽 (feather) — a wing is covered in feathers.
支 (zhī) gives a sound fairly close to chì, sharing a similar rhyme.
⺼ (flesh) — 膀 names a part of the body.
旁 (beside) contributes to the character's form, describing something at the body's side, like the upper arm or a wing.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟张开翅膀飞走了。
example.pinyin: nà zhī niǎo zhāngkāi chìbǎng fēizǒule.
example.english: That bird spread its wings and flew away.
example.fact: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, up to 3.5 meters, which lets it glide for hours over the open ocean on rising air currents without flapping — some individuals have been tracked flying over 10,000 kilometers in a single foraging trip.

components.note: 丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'
尸 (a bent human figure) — 尼 originally pictured two people standing close together, related to the idea of nearness.
匕 (a reversed person) — paired with 尸, giving the sense of closeness; the character was later borrowed for its sound to write 'nun' and to transliterate foreign names and places.

尔 is the simplified form of 爾, an ancient pictograph whose original image (possibly a decorative net or woven pattern) is unclear; it was borrowed early on as the second-person pronoun 'you' and is now used mainly as a phonetic syllable in transliterated names.

example.hanzi: 丹尼尔昨天搬到了这个城市。
example.pinyin: dānní'ěr zuótiān bāndàole zhège chéngshì.
example.english: Daniel moved to this city yesterday.
example.fact: The biblical figure Daniel is said to have survived a night in a den of lions unharmed; historically, lions were once common across the Middle East and Southern Europe, and the last wild Asiatic lion within that historic range wasn't wiped out until the early 20th century.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 掌 names the palm, part of the hand.
尚 (shàng) gives a rhyme close to zhǎng, with the initial shifted.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后,现场爆发出热烈的掌声。
example.pinyin: yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, xiànchǎng bàofā chū rèliè de zhǎngshēng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience burst into warm applause.
example.fact: Physicists studying applause have found that when an audience claps enthusiastically, individual clappers unconsciously synchronize their rhythm for a few seconds, then deliberately break apart into randomness again because irregular clapping actually sounds louder overall — a pattern first documented in a study of Eastern European theater crowds.

components.note: 木 here is reused from 桀 (jié), the original phonetic component of the traditional form 傑, retaining a sound close to jié.
灬 (fire) replaces the traditional form's 舛 (a pair of feet) in this simplification and no longer carries independent meaning — the simplified shape stands in for 傑, meaning 'outstanding, heroic.'
王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 瑞 describes a jade tablet used as a token of good fortune.
耑 (duān) gives a sound distantly related to ruì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 杰瑞养了一只可爱的猫。
example.pinyin: jiéruì yǎngle yī zhī kě'ài de māo.
example.english: Jerry has a cute cat.
example.fact: The cartoon mouse Jerry, star of the classic 'Tom and Jerry' shorts, was almost named 'Jinx' before animators settled on Jerry — the series went on to win seven Academy Awards for Best Animated Short Film, tying it with Looney Tunes for the most in that category.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.
尸 (a body) — the body of an animal.
毛 (fur/hair) — trailing behind it, together giving 尾 its meaning 'tail.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影的结尾让人意外。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéwěi ràng rén yìwài.
example.english: The ending of this movie is surprising.
example.fact: In music, a 'coda' — from the Italian word for 'tail' — is a passage that brings a piece to a formal close after its main themes have finished; Beethoven was especially known for writing unusually long codas, sometimes nearly as long as a movement's main body, to give his symphonies a more dramatic conclusion.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅因为牛肉面而有名。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng yīnwèi niúròumiàn ér yǒumíng.
example.english: This restaurant is famous for its beef noodle soup.
example.fact: In 1968, artist Andy Warhol predicted that 'in the future, everyone will be famous for 15 minutes' — a line written for an exhibition catalogue that, decades before social media, anticipated how easily ordinary people could achieve brief viral fame.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'

example.hanzi: 事情的发展完全出乎我们的预料。
example.pinyin: shìqíng de fāzhǎn wánquán chūhū wǒmen de yùliào.
example.english: The development of the matter was completely beyond our expectations.
example.fact: Modern five-day weather forecasts are now roughly as accurate as one-day forecasts were in the 1980s, an improvement driven by satellite data, supercomputers, and better mathematical models of the atmosphere.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù

example.hanzi: 我们开车走高速去了那个城市。
example.pinyin: wǒmen kāichē zǒu gāosù qùle nàge chéngshì.
example.english: We drove on the expressway to that city.
example.fact: NASA's Parker Solar Probe is the fastest human-made object ever built, reaching speeds of over 690,000 kilometers per hour as it dives close to the Sun — fast enough to travel from New York to Los Angeles in about 21 seconds.

meanings: variant of 贊同|赞同[zan4 tong2]

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 大多数股东都赞同这项计划。
example.pinyin: dà duōshù gǔdōng dōu zàntóng zhè xiàng jìhuà.
example.english: Most shareholders agree with this plan.
example.fact: Switzerland holds more national referendums than any other country, with citizens voting on dozens of proposals covering everything from immigration policy to tunnel construction — a direct-democracy tradition dating back to the 19th century.

meanings: variant of 合併|合并[he2 bing4]

components.note: 合 pictures a lid (亼) fitting neatly down over a container's mouth (口) — the image of two matching parts joining together, the source of 合's meaning 'to close, to combine, to fit.'
并 (simplified from 並) depicts two people standing side by side — giving its meaning of 'together' or 'and.'

example.hanzi: 两家公司决定合并成一家。
example.pinyin: liǎng jiā gōngsī juédìng hébìng chéng yī jiā.
example.english: The two companies decided to merge into one.
example.fact: At Manaus, Brazil, the dark waters of the Rio Negro and the pale, sediment-rich Amazon River merge but do not fully mix for several kilometers downstream, flowing side by side in a visible line known as the 'meeting of waters' due to differences in temperature, speed, and density.

meanings: stylized gait used by performers on stage

components.note: 厶 (a curled shape, originally 'self' or a cocoon-like form) sits above 口 (mouth) in 台's ancient form, an image once linked to being pleased; the character was later borrowed for its sound to mean 'platform, stage,' and even 'typhoon' (in 台风).
口 (mouth) completes the original picture beneath 厶, before the character's meaning shifted entirely away from its ancient sense.
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 演员在台上走台步显得格外优雅。
example.pinyin: yǎnyuán zài tái shàng zǒu táibù xiǎnde géwài yōuyǎ.
example.english: The actor's stage walk appeared especially graceful.
example.fact: Peking opera, formalized in the late 18th century, trains performers for years in stylized walks, gestures, and acrobatics before they ever take a lead role — a single sleeve toss or turn can take months of repetitive drilling to master.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 这部话剧下周将在剧院上演。
example.pinyin: zhè bù huàjù xià zhōu jiāng zài jùyuàn shàngyǎn.
example.english: This play will be staged at the theater next week.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Globe Theatre, built in London in 1599, could hold around 3,000 spectators standing and seated around an open-air stage; after burning down in 1613 when a cannon effect during a performance of Henry VIII set the thatched roof alight, it was rebuilt within a year.

components.note: 乂 (a hand holding a writing tool) — the act of recording events, giving 史 its meaning 'history, chronicle.'
艹 (plant) — 蒂 names the stem that attaches a fruit or flower to its plant.
帝 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 蒂.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 史蒂夫是我们公司的技术总监。
example.pinyin: shǐdìfū shì wǒmen gōngsī de jìshù zǒngjiān.
example.english: Steve is our company's technical director.
example.fact: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in his parents' garage in Los Altos, California in 1976, and that same garage was later designated a historic site by the city, even though the company quickly outgrew it and moved to larger offices within a couple of years.

components.note: 用 is thought to depict a wooden bucket or fence-like container; being useful for practical tasks connects the picture to 用's meaning 'to use, to employ.'

于's ancient form is thought to picture a curling breath of air or a bent stick, once used to write a sighing exclamation; that concrete image faded as the character became the grammatical preposition 'at, in, to.'

example.hanzi: 这种材料主要用于建筑行业。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng cáiliào zhǔyào yòngyú jiànzhù hángyè.
example.english: This material is mainly used in the construction industry.
example.fact: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, is roughly 200 times stronger than steel by weight and is being explored for use in everything from flexible electronics to water filtration membranes since its isolation was first demonstrated in 2004.

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.hanzi: 她凭优异的成绩获得了全额奖学金。
example.pinyin: tā píng yōuyì de chéngjì huòdéle quán'é jiǎngxuéjīn.
example.english: She earned a full scholarship with her excellent grades.
example.fact: The Rhodes Scholarship, one of the oldest and most prestigious international graduate scholarships, was established in 1902 through the will of British businessman Cecil Rhodes and funds recipients from dozens of countries to study at the University of Oxford.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伊 originally referred to a person
尹 (yǐn) gives a sound close to 伊's reading yī, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
丽 is the simplified form of 麗, which depicted the ornate antlers of a deer (鹿) — a fitting image behind its meaning 'beautiful, magnificent.'
艹 (grass) — 莎 originally named a type of sedge grass.
沙 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 莎.
Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'

example.hanzi: 伊丽莎白是这个小镇上最受欢迎的老师。
example.pinyin: yīlìshābái shì zhège xiǎozhèn shàng zuì shòu huānyíng de lǎoshī.
example.english: Elizabeth is the most popular teacher in this small town.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for over 70 years, longer than any other British monarch, and during her lifetime she met more than half of all US presidents ever elected, from Harry Truman through Joe Biden.

components.note: 玉 (jade, shown without its dot) represents something valuable.
厶 beneath suggests something slipping away privately, giving 丢 its meaning 'to lose, to throw away.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 在这么多人面前摔倒真是太丢人了。
example.pinyin: zài zhème duō rén miànqián shuāidǎo zhēnshi tài diūrén le.
example.english: Falling in front of so many people is really embarrassing.
example.fact: Blushing is the only human expression that Charles Darwin himself called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions' — unlike most emotional reactions, it can't be consciously suppressed, because it's controlled by the sympathetic nervous system rather than muscles we can voluntarily control.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
事 pictures a hand holding a forked stick used as an official tally or record-keeping tool, tying the character to its meanings 'affair, matter' and 'to serve.'

example.hanzi: 他做事一向很认真。
example.pinyin: tā zuòshì yīxiàng hěn rènzhēn.
example.english: He has always been very serious about handling matters.
example.fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time needed to build a Model T from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes, a leap in efficiency that transformed manufacturing worldwide and helped make car ownership affordable for millions.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

example.hanzi: 这个国家目前正处在经济转型期。
example.pinyin: zhège guójiā mùqián zhèng chǔzài jīngjì zhuǎnxíng qī.
example.english: This country is currently in a period of economic transition.
example.fact: Istanbul is the only major city in the world situated on two continents, with the Bosphorus Strait splitting it between Europe and Asia — a geographic position that has made it a strategic crossroads for trade and empires for over 2,500 years.

components.note: 人 — a person, shown bending over
贝 (money/shell) — a heavy load of money the person is carrying on their back
责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 请联系项目负责人确认时间。
example.pinyin: qǐng liánxì xiàngmù fùzérén quèrèn shíjiān.
example.english: Please contact the person in charge of the project to confirm the time.
example.fact: During the 1970 Apollo 13 crisis, flight director Gene Kranz — the person in charge of NASA's Mission Control — refused to accept that the crew could not be brought home safely, coordinating an improvised carbon-dioxide scrubber fix built entirely from materials already onboard the spacecraft.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

example.hanzi: 在美国吃饭通常需要给小费。
example.pinyin: zài měiguó chīfàn tōngcháng xūyào gěi xiǎofèi.
example.english: When dining in the US, you usually need to give a tip.
example.fact: Tipping is believed to have originated in the taverns of 17th-century England, where patrons paid extra 'to insure promptness'; the custom later spread through Europe and was brought back to the United States by wealthy Americans returning from Grand Tours, though it remains far less common in many other countries today.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
立 (to stand) — 端 relates to standing upright, being straight and proper.
耑 (duān) gives the sound — an exact match with 端.

example.hanzi: 沙漠地区的气温变化十分极端。
example.pinyin: shāmò dìqū de qìwēn biànhuà shífēn jíduān.
example.english: Temperature changes in desert regions are extremely extreme.
example.fact: The Lut Desert in Iran holds the record for the hottest land surface temperature ever measured by satellite, 80.8°C (177°F) in 2005, even though virtually no one lives there to experience it directly.

meanings: intern (esp. a student in practical training)

components.note: 实 is the simplified form of 實, which showed 宀 (a roof) over 毌 (strung-together cowry shells) and 貝 (money) — a house full of valuables, giving 实 its meaning 'real, solid, substantial.' The simplified bottom shape no longer pictures the shells directly.

习 is the simplified form of 習, which showed 羽 (feathers/wings) above 日 (the sun) — a young bird flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly, the source of 习's meaning 'to practice, to study, custom.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 这个暑假她在一家科技公司当实习生。
example.pinyin: zhège shǔjià tā zài yī jiā kējì gōngsī dāng shíxíshēng.
example.english: This summer she is interning at a tech company.
example.fact: The modern internship traces back to medieval guild apprenticeships, where young people trained for years under a master craftsman before being allowed to work independently — apprenticeships for goldsmiths in medieval London, for instance, could last as long as seven years.

components.note: 一 (one) is used here as a simple graphic base for the character.
从 (cóng) gives the exact sound of 丛.
木 (tree), doubled — two trees side by side depict a cluster of trees, the source of 林's meaning 'forest, grove.'

example.hanzi: 探险队深入丛林寻找失落的古城。
example.pinyin: tànxiǎnduì shēnrù cónglín xúnzhǎo shīluò de gǔchéng.
example.english: The expedition team went deep into the jungle looking for the lost ancient city.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest covers less than 1% of Earth's land surface yet is home to roughly 10% of all known species, and scientists still discover new species there at a rate of about one every two days.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 国会将就这项法案举行听证会。
example.pinyin: guóhuì jiāng jiù zhè xiàng fǎ'àn jǔxíng tīngzhènghuì.
example.english: Congress will hold a hearing on this bill.
example.fact: The 1973 Watergate hearings in the US Senate were broadcast live on television for months, and an estimated 85% of American households tuned in to at least part of the coverage — one of the first times a congressional hearing became mass entertainment.

components.note: 木 here is reused from 桀 (jié), the original phonetic component of the traditional form 傑, retaining a sound close to jié.
灬 (fire) replaces the traditional form's 舛 (a pair of feet) in this simplification and no longer carries independent meaning — the simplified shape stands in for 傑, meaning 'outstanding, heroic.'
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'

example.hanzi: 杰西每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: jiéxī měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: Jesse goes for a run in the park every morning.
example.fact: Sprinter Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, held under Nazi Germany, directly undermining the regime's propaganda about racial superiority in front of a home crowd of 110,000 spectators.

components.note: 干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 公司即将发布年度财报。
example.pinyin: gōngsī jíjiāng fābù niándù cáibào.
example.english: The company is about to release its annual financial report.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar, adopted in 1582, adds a leap day nearly every four years to keep pace with Earth's actual orbit of about 365.2422 days — but it skips the leap day in century years not divisible by 400, which is why the year 2000 had one but 1900 and 2100 do not.

components.note: 刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — cutting and arranging pieces in order ties to 列's meaning 'row, line, to arrange'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 这辆列车将在十分钟后进站。
example.pinyin: zhè liàng lièchē jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu jìnzhàn.
example.english: This train will arrive at the station in ten minutes.
example.fact: Japan's experimental L0 series maglev train set the world speed record for rail vehicles in 2015, reaching 603 km/h (374 mph) during a test run near Mount Fuji, using magnetic levitation to eliminate friction with the rails.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 我从他的表情看出他很紧张。
example.pinyin: wǒ cóng tā de biǎoqíng kànchū tā hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: I could tell from his expression that he was very nervous.
example.fact: Psychologist Paul Ekman's research in the 1960s found that certain facial expressions — for emotions like fear, anger, and surprise — are recognized across vastly different cultures, including isolated tribes in Papua New Guinea who had never seen outside media, suggesting these expressions are biologically innate rather than learned.
